6.2.1. Amendment of the landfill replacement reserve. Thank you, Madam Chair. Good morning. My name is Angela Gardner. I'm the General Manager of Utilities Environment Division. And this first report this morning is seeking approval to adjust the expenditure definition in the capital reserve by a to be in alignment with the current practice for the landfill replacement reserve. In 2011, Council approved the landfill optimization report that indicated that without significant changes to the landfill and improvements in waste diversion.

The landfill would only have 10 to 15 years of space remaining. Significant changes were made to extend the life for another 40 years. More recently, the projected operational lifespan of the landfill has been further extended.

Primarily due to a reduction in the volume of waste compared to the previous projections and an improvement in the landfill's compaction rate, which reduces the amount of space required per ton of waste.
In order to bring the bylaw into alignment with current practices for the types of projects that the landfill replacement reserve has been funding since 2011.

And the needs going forward changes are required. This report proposes expanding the scope of the landfill replacement reserve and renaming it to the waste processing capital and replacement reserve to include capital funding for ongoing operations at the landfill, the landfill gas facility and the new organic processing facility.
These facilities require sustained capital investment to support operational needs, and currently there is no dedicated funding source for such projects.
In addition to the bylaw amendments, Council previously approved funding to support the maintenance and rehabilitation of the asphalt pad at the material recovery center.
Due to the limited scope of the landfill replacement reserve, the funds were temporarily placed in the paid roadways infrastructure reserve.
This report is also recommending that once the bylaw changes are made, the funds totaling $179,000 at $200 be transferred to the new reserve.
Our team is available to answer any questions there might have, and that's my introduction.

Thank you Madam Chair. This next report is seeking approval to adopt the proposed framework for waste collection location reviews going forward.
In Saskatoon we currently collect 25% of our curbside waste collections in the back lanes.
As part of the engagement pilot in east view that was reported on earlier this year 82% 82% of residents express the strong preference to keep waste collections in the back lane.
In assessing an approach to review the remaining we're laying collections throughout the city from an operational perspective.
The administration noted that back lane collections account for 84% of all reported safety incidents.
One point eight times more likely to have a by-law infraction related to illegal dumping or other violations.
And are on average 20 to 25% slower to collect than front street collections.

So while there are operational benefits to front street collections in most cases, considering the strong preferences of residents the administration is not recommending pursuing any full neighborhood conversions at this time.
If and when that might be needed, the process to undertake the neighborhood review is outlined in the report.
Having said this, there are locations where there are significant operational challenges with rear lane collection that impact the safe and efficient collection of waste.
To address these situations, the administration has outlined a consistent process that will be followed where necessary.
So this report is seeking Council's approval to adopt the framework for both the operational and neighborhood reviews as outlined in the report.
And if there's any questions, our teams available to answer them. Thank you.

This report provides an update on the relocation and upgrades of the Saskatoon Fire Department's Dispatch Center,
Highlighting McKie Miles, Thones, and Software Enhancements.
In February of 2025, the Dispatch Center successfully transitioned its operations from station one to the newly renovated station nine.
The upgraded facility now houses 18 call takers and dispatchers across four battalions,
along with the assistant deputy chief of emergency communications.
This move marks a significance that forward in modernizing emergency response infrastructure.
A major component of this project was updating the network from analog to digital...
Analog to digital to support the nationwide transition to NG 911.
This upgrade was completed well ahead of the Canadian radio television and telecommunications commissions,
or CRTC, mandated deadline, making Saskatoon Fire Department the 20th out of more than 200 public safety answering points in Canada to complete the transition.
Extensive work and training are ongoing in preparation for the full deployment of computer-aided dispatch system,
and advance call taking software, which is scheduled for early 2026.
These upgrades will significantly enhance operational efficiency and response capabilities.
From inception to completion, the entire project's band approximately six years involving multiple phases of planning, construction, technology, integration, and staff training.
The Saskatoon Fire Department would like to extend sincere thanks to the many city staff across various departments who contributed their expertise,
dedication and collaborative spirit to this initiative.
